newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Volatility steady in small caps.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Volatility steady in small caps.

text.p: Volatilities and premiums in S&P 100 .OEX and S&P 500 .SPX stock index options stayed high Thursday as the market extended record-setting gains, while the small-capitalization sector remained largely ignored.
Small-cap stocks have largely avoided the sharp intraday swings their blue chip counterparts see almost every day, and some options traders see an opportunity there.
The S&P 600 small-cap index .SML is a possibiliby "for those looking for a little bit more protection and who can give up these crazy, wild moves," said Bill Yates at DYR Associates.
Yates said the index is particularly attractive to investors expecting a sharp decline in major indices.
"Small cap is where there's less risk," he said. "There's less risk because there's a lower implied volatility, and there's less risk because they haven't gone up as much."
In the OEX, for example, implied volatility has risen to the 20 area over the last few weeks from the 12 to 16 region where it spent much of last year.
Implied volatility on the SML has been holding steady around the 23 level, he said.
"It's staying about where it usually is, but now implied volatility in the blue chips has ratcheted up," Yates said.
"That shows there's a little more risk," he said. "We look at it as the market's opinion on the riskiness of the market.
"That's gone up while small caps have stayed the same."
At 1150 CST/1750 GMT, the SML was up 1.15 at 147.13. Its record high was 149.06, struck on January 23.
Another index of small cap stocks, the Russell 2000 index .RUT, was up 2.37 at 367.77. Its all-time high, also reached on January 23, was 373.17.
Options trading in both indices was thin Thursday, with the heaviest volume in the RUT February 360 put, which traded 1,000 contracts.
The February 365, 370 and 375 calls traded a total of 45 contracts.
The February 365 put rose 1-1/8 to six and the February 370 added 13/16 to 3-1/8.
In the SML, the February 145 calls were bid at 2-7/8 and offered at 3-1/4. The February 150 calls were bid at 3/16 and offered at 7/16.
Among broader indices, traders said options activity was moderate as the market extended Wednesday's sharp gains.
The OEX was up 5.10 at 788.24 after closing at a record 783.14 Wednesday, and the SPX gained 5.70 to 808.47. It ended at a record 802.77 Wednesday.
The busiest OEX option was the February 760 put, which traded more than 7,800 contracts. It lost 3/4 to 1-7/8.
With volume of about 7,000, the February 790 call was the most active OEX call. It rose 1-3/4 to eight.
In the SPX, the most volume was in the February 800 call, where about 6,725 contracts changed hands. ((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
